newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian bond spreads narrow to US, Canada.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian bond spreads narrow to US, Canada.

text.p: Australian bond spreads narrowed to North American bonds as the local market pushed ahead despite the flat to softer close in the U.S. overnight.
Traders said there was good buying interest across the whole curve in the morning session that saw the curve hold steady and spreads narrow from the open.
Bonds gave up some of their morning gains as the A$600 million of stock from today's tender was absorbed into the market, but they still managed to finish up on the day.
The curves finished slightly steeper after the long end, which had kept pace with short end gains during the morning, softened a touch in afternoon trading.

A strong tone to the New Zealand market saw spreads reverse an initial narrowing by the close. Eurokiwi and samurai issues were supporting the short end, and the long end was being aided by bullish sentiment ahead of Friday's December quarter CPI.
Traders said the 110 points on the yield curve seemed to be providing good resistance, even though the short end was supported by ongoing expectations of a rate cut.
"It makes it easier for us to try and push lengthening trades, and that's what people have been doing," said one trader of the recent curve steepening.
But while he had thought the steepening towards 110 points was "illogical, irrational," others had felt the curve could have gone to 115 or 120 points today.
"I thought it would actually do better, relatively, today, but that early buying in the 10-years has seen the tens do a bit of catch up on the day," another trader said.
"I'm starting to have my doubts, though, because I think the market overall looks pretty positive, and...the risk is now that in the short term 10-years will actually outperform the threes."
U.S. CPI and retail trade data later today will provide direction for bonds, with traders saying the local market's best chance of outperforming was in a bear market.
